configs.purpose: one planted fault at a time in the fixture pool, each of which must fail the gate: the anchor (its ID, registration, file name, stage, class, medium, scheduling, KCs, its "based on" card with its incident, date, date marks and source and without code, spine 6.2's key-run cell, the pair, the anchor's class on a flawed member, the variants field); the cases (form, id, duplicates, keys and acceptable classes, a key that writes primary, a sound key with acceptable classes, acceptable classes that are not a list, statement, texts); typed evidence (missing, of the wrong type, without its artifact, a sound case's restatement with no scenarios or two while three pass, no load-bearing lines or four, malformed, out of range or repeated ones, line-anchored evidence on three lines while four pass); key runs and key lines (missing, not a run ID, not on disk, malformed, empty, not stated, stated only inside a word, not stated in the configuration named); the keying battery (another class or a subclass of the case's, a flawed case keyed sound, an acceptable set narrower, wider, or of the same size with another class, another evidence type, load-bearing lines that differ, hold one line more or hold part of the core, a vacuous sound case, unknown, no port, no key, no battery, a variant whose statement, diff or receipt drifted, or whose statement gained a blank first line, while a faithful regenerate passes, and the case as the battery receives it); the key's shape (keys that spell their lines loadBearing, flawed keys without evidence, with evidence null or without its type, with their acceptable classes as text or as numbers, or with an empty class, G2 keys without their recomputed lines or with their lines as numbers, sound keys without their primary class); exemplars (five while exactly six pass, one shared label, relabeled copies, copies that differ only in white space, copies re-seeded in decimal literals or in every literal form README section 3 names, a flipped sign included, empty variants lists); pending declarations (variants on an anchor that ships with them, done or unknown tasks, a re-keying with no task, malformed or without a key run, a re-key still pending once its engine has a port); variants (no pair, no sound form, two claims, no operator, an operator the spine does not list or one that cannot key the class, a generator reference to template t5, to band 4 or with a seed past the uint32 range, while t4, band 3 and seed 2^32 - 1 pass); nine Clearinghouse faults (a naive baseline above its bar, a naive mean exactly at it, a naive mean that meets it though its first and lowest seed does not, a reference below its bar, a reference mean below it though its first and highest seed reaches it, scores that change between executions, reference scores alone that change, no recorded seeds, a score that is not a number), with a reference exactly at its bar passing; --strict on a pending re-key, pending variants and an empty pool; --only naming a missing anchor; and three file faults (a file that does not parse, one that holds no mapping, two files for one anchor). The clean pool must pass, in memory and read from files, with a draft file named with an underscore and a readme beside it

The stand-in battery keys G2 and sound cases by running the box engine (the premises, their smallest unsat subset, the violation query) and reads the other classes from a recorded verdict; it tests the gate, not the classes. The eight cases of AUD-2.2, AUD-2.3, AUD-2.4 and AUD-5.3 wait for their engines' lanes (W2-T01, W3-T05) and are keyed by their executed runs meanwhile.

Exemplars (AUDIT-DESK 4): a flawed case counts only when its label (operator, artifact, medium) is new for its class and its statement, diff and receipt differ from every exemplar counted there once white space is collapsed and numeric literals are replaced; a new label on a counted structure is a finding. The fixture's S1 variants are structurally distinct (six contradictions with their own unsat cores for G2, six arithmetic slips for G4, six inconclusive or bounded results reported as verdicts for G5), and fixture-pool-relabeled-copies plants the copies the rule exists to catch.

fixture-pool-battery-misspelled-lines: the key a battery returns carries primary, also and evidence {type, load_bearing} (README section 4). A battery that returns its lines as loadBearing, the spelling of the case it receives, would otherwise have its lines read as absent and the comparison skipped, so AUD-1.1's wrong lines would pass; the gate fails on each flawed key whose evidence it cannot read.

mutants: each mutant of scripts/spikes/W1-T40/mutants.mjs replaces one exact piece of the gate's source in a scratch copy, which weakens one rule that the gate's header, the README or the spine names (those named *-strict make it stricter instead, failing a valid value at the edge of a rule), and runs the gate's self-check; every one must make it fail. The list holds one plain weakening per rule and per edge, not every weakening a rule admits.
